knowledge:
- key_parameters: ambiguityThreshold=Position-wise detection level for ambiguous bases in consensusProfile() (0 to 0.2, default 0). Lower values catch all variation but increase degeneracy; higher values capture major variation but may miss rare variants ;; designStrategyPrimer=Strategy for primer design in designOligos(), either "ambiguous" (default) or "mixed" (CODEHOP-like, shorter degenerate 3' end and longer consensus 5' end) ;; maxGapFrequency=Maximum gap frequency in the alignment for primers and probes in designOligos() (default 0.01) ;; maxDegeneracyPrimer/maxDegeneracyProbe=Maximum degeneracy allowed for primers/probes in designOligos() (default 4) ;; length=Amplicon length range in designAssays() (default c(65, 120)) ;; tmDifferencePrimers=Maximum allowed difference between the mean Tm of forward and reverse primers in designAssays() (default NULL)
- alternatives: The documentation mentions using other external software to evaluate primer-dimers, hairpin structures, and cross-reactivity with non-targets. It also relies on Biostrings for alignment import (readDNAMultipleAlignment) and masking (colmask, rowmask, gapmask)
- when_to_use: Appropriate for designing degenerate primers, probes, and qPCR assays for highly sequence-variable targets (such as RNA viruses) from a multiple DNA sequence alignment
- pitfalls: If no oligos or assays are found, the user may need to increase ambiguityThreshold in consensusProfile() or relax design constraints (e.g., degeneracy, Tm, GC content) ;; Matching primer Tm is noted as a flawed strategy; what matters is the amount of primer bound at the annealing temperature (ta) ;; checkMatch() is slow with many target sequences; it is recommended to run it on a subset of candidates ;; Ambiguous bases and gaps in target sequences are identified as mismatches by checkMatch(), and false negatives/positives can occur due to poorly aligned sequences ;; checkMatch() does not specify which strand (minus or plus) the oligo matches to, which is critical for single-stranded targets

workflows.name: standard_oligo_assay_design
workflows.intent: Design degenerate primers, probes, and qPCR assays from a multiple DNA sequence alignment using the default ambiguous strategy.
input: example_alignment.txt (Multiple DNA sequence alignment in FASTA format)
workflows.stages: 1. Import alignment using readDNAMultipleAlignment() ;; 2. Generate consensus profile using consensusProfile() ;; 3. Design oligos using designOligos() ;; 4. Design assays using designAssays() ;; 5. Check matches against target sequences using checkMatch() ;; 6. Visualize data using plotData() ;; 7. Export results to CSV and FASTA format
workflows.code:
library(rprimer)
library(Biostrings)
filepath <- system.file("extdata", "example_alignment.txt", package = "rprimer")
myAlignment <- readDNAMultipleAlignment(filepath, format = "fasta")
myConsensusProfile <- consensusProfile(myAlignment, ambiguityThreshold = 0.05)
plotData(myConsensusProfile)
selection <- myConsensusProfile[
  myConsensusProfile$position >= 5000 & myConsensusProfile$position <= 5800, 
  ]
plotData(selection)
myOligos <- designOligos(myConsensusProfile)
myOligos$sequence[[1]]
myOligos$gcContent[[1]]
myOligos$tm[[1]]
plotData(myOligos)
bestOligoScore <- min(myOligos$score)
oligoSelection <- myOligos[myOligos$score == bestOligoScore, ]
bindingRegion <- myConsensusProfile[
  myConsensusProfile$position >= oligoSelection[1, ]$start & 
    myConsensusProfile$position <= oligoSelection[1, ]$end,
  ]
plotData(bindingRegion, type = "nucleotide")
myAssays <- designAssays(myOligos)
plotData(myAssays)
bestAssayScore <- min(myAssays$score)
myAssaySelection <- myAssays[myAssays$score == bestAssayScore, ]
from <- myAssaySelection[1, ]$start
to <- myAssaySelection[1, ]$end
plotData(myConsensusProfile, highlight = c(from, to))
myAssayRegion <- myConsensusProfile[
  myConsensusProfile$position >= from & 
    myConsensusProfile$position <= to, 
]
plotData(myAssayRegion, type = "nucleotide")
paste(myAssayRegion$iupac, collapse = "")
oligoSelectionMatch <- checkMatch(oligoSelection[1:3, ], target = myAlignment)
oligoSelectionMatch$idOneMismatch[[1]]
plotData(oligoSelectionMatch)
as(myOligos[1:2, ], "DNAStringSet")
as(myAssays[1:2, ], "DNAStringSet")
write.csv(myAssays, file = "myAssays.csv", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
write.table(myAssays, file = "myAssays.txt", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
toFile <- as(myOligos[1:2, ], "DNAStringSet")
writeXStringSet(toFile, file = "myOligos.txt")

workflows.name: mixed_primer_design_masked_alignment
workflows.intent: Design longer, low-degeneracy primers using the mixed (CODEHOP-like) strategy targeting specific masked regions of a multiple DNA sequence alignment.
input: example_alignment.txt (Multiple DNA sequence alignment in FASTA format)
workflows.stages: 1. Import alignment using readDNAMultipleAlignment() ;; 2. Mask non-target regions using colmask() ;; 3. Generate consensus profile of the masked alignment using consensusProfile() ;; 4. Design mixed primers (without probes) using designOligos() with modified settings ;; 5. Visualize the designed mixed primers using plotData()
workflows.code:
library(rprimer)
library(Biostrings)
filepath <- system.file("extdata", "example_alignment.txt", package = "rprimer")
myAlignment <- readDNAMultipleAlignment(filepath, format = "fasta")
myMaskedAlignment <- myAlignment
colmask(myMaskedAlignment, invert = TRUE) <- c(3000:4000, 5000:6000)
myMaskedConsensusProfile <- consensusProfile(myMaskedAlignment, ambiguityThreshold = 0.05)
myMaskedMixedPrimers <- designOligos(myMaskedConsensusProfile,
                                     maxDegeneracyPrimer = 8,
                                     lengthPrimer = c(24:28),
                                     tmPrimer = c(65,70),
                                     designStrategyPrimer = "mixed", 
                                     probe = FALSE)
plotData(myMaskedMixedPrimers)
